request: Design the replacement event counter API. Return sketches and a rationale; stop before implementation. Evaluate both submitted sketches, propose a candidate, then assess the separate implementation diary and report the next workflow steps. This is a bounded template exercise; do not launch other agents or pretend an Arena round happened.

grounding.read_pattern: Callers request counts by actor and event type. Event-type lookups dominate at about one million events; no full event scan is acceptable per lookup.
grounding.write_pattern: Independent actors each own an append-only event stream; reads combine streams.
grounding.boundary: Incoming JSON wire payloads use type_tag/count_value; callers consume domain EventKind and Count. All consumers are internal and can migrate together.
grounding.invariants: Event kinds are declared in the schema. A new kind must be handled by counters and serialization. No external compatibility contract exists.

candidate_a: Public API record(WireMessage): boolean; countFor(kind): Count scans every actor event list. UI passes raw type_tag/count_value. Everyone writes shared mutable totals under a global lock. Requests pass UI -> facade -> manager -> service -> registry -> adapter -> store across seven files. Keep both legacy and new counter APIs indefinitely. Maintain SUPPORTED_KINDS by hand beside schema enum.
candidate_b: Public API record(actor, kind, amount): void, countFor(actor, kind): Count; per-actor maps index domain kind to totals, combined at snapshot reads. Parse wire payloads in ingestion. Public facade and pure count operations in one module; storage module is private. Derive serialization variants from the schema. Migrate all internal callers and delete old API.

implementation_diary.deviation: Importers must cast WireMessage as unknown as Count to call the counter; wrapper comment tells callers which fields to copy.
Replay also casts wire objects to Count and documents manual field copying; a third adapter is proposed to hide this.

authority: Only /tmp/jstack-design-review-eval/architect/result.md is writable. The diary is a hypothetical separate run. Do not modify target implementation.
